sources behind the Persian epic tradition, and recounts Firdusi's life, his work on the Shah Nameh, his association with Mahmud of Ghazna, his disappointment over payment, his wanderings, and the story of his death and delayed reward.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The passage states that Arabs conquered Persia, that Merv fell that despite Turkish speech at court and the universal use of Arabic script, the older Persian temper still lived on.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The passage says Ormuzd was replaced by Allah and Ahriman by Satan.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"It says Persia's past was kept alive in the myth-loving mind of the people, in poets' songs, and in minstrels' lays, producing a continuing opposition of Persian to Arab.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The fall of the Umayyid dynasty and the rise of separate dynasties in Spain, Sicily, Egypt, and Tunis are said to have strengthened Persian desire to preserve historical individuality and ancient traditions.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The passage states that Firdusi was not the first collector of old Persian epic material and names the Avesta, oral transmission, the Zarer, the History of King Ardeshir, and chronicles of Persian kings as earlier sources.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"It singles out the Chodainameh of Dihkan Danishwar, says it was written in middle-Persian in Pahlavi writing, and says Abu Mansur later had a neo-Persian Shah Nameh prepared, after which Dakiki versified a thousand lines of it.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The passage says Firdusi was born in Tus in A.D. 935 and uses a garden-and-flowers image to describe his gathering of Persian imaginative material.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:4","ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"It says Firdusi had been working on his epic since 971, dedicated it in 999 to Ahmad ibn the passage, Mahmud had promised a gold dirhem a line but sent sixty thousand silver ones, which Firdusi rejected and distributed before leaving.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The passage says Firdusi later wrote a bitter lampoon against Mahmud, that a friend bought it off, and that Firdusi wandered through Herat, Taberistan, and Baghdad, where he composed Yusuf and Salikha.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"It says Firdusi returned to Tus to die, hospice.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Firdusi","description":"Poet born in Tus in A.D. 935, compiler of the Persian epic tradition, elves.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker repeatedly addresses Loddfafnir with advice and says hearing and learning it bring paradisal and infernal imagery.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker asks the breeze to greet the cypress, basil, and rose on tavern.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The poem advises friendliness to men of God and cites Noah's ark and the questioned.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The addressee called the 'Moon of Kanaan' is told that the Egyptian throne pertains to them and that the time has come to leave chains.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The speaker contrasts the cloister and cowl with the Magian's cloister and pure wine, while remembering days of union.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Dust from the addressee's threshold is said to balm the speaker's eyes, and the heart is warned about a pit near the chin's fair apple.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"At evening a musician plays a reed melody, and the speaker says earthly things grew gray to tearful eyes.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"A youth fills the bowl with wine, and the speaker says the cup brought deliverance from Being's prison.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"In dialogue, a stranger seeks grace from the 'Monarch of the lovely' and is told to let the beloved go.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The beloved's locks are said to hold souls in fetters, and a wine-reflected crimson tint appears on the wine.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The beloved's love is said to freshen Rizvn's gardens, while the beloved's absence intensifies Gehenna's and swear that he will have her for his own.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"In the same paraphrase, Brynhild says she would rather have Sigurth than any other oath-breaker.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"One interpolated passage is summarized as warning that if someone falsely taunts a man for silence, he should kill text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Editorial notes on early stanzas of Völuspá explain the völva's compelled reply to Othin, enumerate the nine worlds and Yggdrasil, describe Ymir and Ginnunga-gap, identify Bur's sons and Midgard, mention the sun and moon, Ithavoll, giant-maids or Norns, and discuss the dwarf catalogue, Dvalin's magic runes, and a story of dwarfs leaving rocks and mountains for the sands.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The note says the völva or wise-woman is called upon by Othin, answers him, and speaks unwillingly because she is compelled by his magic power.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The note lists nine worlds, including worlds of gods, Wanes, elves, men, giants, fire, dark elves, the dead, and an uncertain ninth world for dwarfs.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Yggdrasil is identified as the world-ash and is said to symbolize the universe.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The note says Ymir is the giant out of whose body the gods made the world and mentions the yawning gap Ginnunga-gap.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The note glosses Bur's sons as Othin, Vili, and Ve, and Mithgarth as the world of men.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The note says the leek was used as a symbol of fine growth and was also supposed to have magic power.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The sun and moon are presented as daughter and son of Mundilferi.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Ithavoll is identified as the meeting-place of the gods.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The note says the giant-maids may be the three great Norns corresponding to the three fates, but it also allows that a lost passage may once have explained them differently.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The notes treat stanzas 9-16 as a catalogue of dwarfs, mention Brimir and Blain as uncertain figures or names, and note that Durin is singled out as authority for the list.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The note says Dvalin gave magic feat.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The king of Rm customarily gave a splendid banquet when his daughters came of age and invited When Slim and Tr send treasure, a gold crown, and a plea for pardon and peace, Feridn seats Minchihr beside him, rejects any exchange of blood for gold, shows the envoy his champions, and declares magnanimity.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Narmn was killed during an earlier attack on an enchanted fort situated on Mount Sipund when the besieged threw down a Ecclesiastes.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The passage says Firdusi worked from written materials and gave the great epic freshness not fanatical.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The verses are said to have remained a delight of the Persians even as Mahmud is described as forgotten by his descendants.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Omar is presented as a boyhood friend of Nizam al-Mulk and Ibn Fitzgerald's burial place.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The passage credits Abu Said of Khorasan, not Omar, with inventing the quatrain form and says he used it to express mystic pantheism.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Omar is said to have been persecuted for want of orthodoxy, while his grave is still honored Gdarz dreams where the hidden prince Kai-khosru is kept and sends Gw to recover him. After a difficult secret journey, Gw recognizes the youth at a fountain by signs of lineage, reunites him with Ferangs, secures horses for their flight, and defeats Kulbd's pursuing force while escorting Kai-khosru and his mother toward Irn.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Afrsiyb learns that his realm and throne have been plundered and that the land has been scorched with fire and sword.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Afrsiyb tells his warriors that vengeance will come and says farewell to joy until that time.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Rustem had already sent people into remote Tartary to look for Kai-khosru.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Gdarz sees the young prince in a dream, learns his location, and is told that Gw is destined to restore him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Gw travels with successive guides, kills each guide to prevent discovery, and continues through harsh terrain with little food or rest.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Gw meets men sent by Prn-wsah in search of Kai-khosru, hides his own purpose, and learns their route.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Gw finds a youth beside a fountain with a cup in his hand, and the two recognize one another.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Gw confirms the youth's identity by seeing a bodily mark inherited from the race of Kai-kobd.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Ferangs urges immediate departure, and Gw captures Behzd and another horse from a meadow before the party sets out for Irn.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Afrsiyb sends Kulbd with three hundred horsemen after the fugitives.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"While Kai-khosru and Ferangs sleep, Gw arms himself, mounts Behzd, attacks the pursuers alone, and routs continue their journey.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:12","ev:13"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Afrsiyb","description":"Ruler who laments the ruin of his realm and later He captures Barz alive, and after a larger battle the Turanian side retreats. Kai-khosru orders Barz executed, but Rustem has him spared and sent away. Barz's mother Shh-r uses a singing-girl in Rustem's household to send him a ring hidden in food, then a file and horses, enabling his escape by night with the two women. Rustem later encounters them, attempts to poison Barz through food, but the mother warns her son; the singing-girl eats and dies, and Barz denounces Rustem's treachery.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Both armies are drawn up again, and Barz rides forward to resume
